title: Forge run manifest v4
description: v3's bytes plus one optional 'realms' property: the world the run was invoked into, pinned by content hash AND embedded verbatim. Absent when the run was invoked with no map, so a run in an unmapped workspace stores and exports the exact v1/v3 shape. The manifest rides inside the run/started payload, which is why embedding it here — rather than widening the event vocabulary — makes 'what world did this run believe in?' answerable from the journal alone, forever, whatever later became of the file. Resume compares only the BUNDLE manifest, so a pinned world never makes a run unresumable.

files.description: bundle-relative path -> sha256 hex digest of file bytes

agents.description: Unchanged from run-manifest.v3: invocation site ('seat', 'seat:member', 'seat:step', 'seat:step:member') -> the pinned resolution. This key is also the pin that replaces the manifest.files entry a charter loses by living in the shared library rather than the bundle directory.

adapter_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of {provider -> adapter file digest} for EVERY provider the chain consulted, not only the chosen one: the capability checks that admitted this chain depended on all of them.

chain.description: The agent's ordered preference chain of abstract model names, as written.

chosen_index.description: Load-bearing: a 'model' field alone never says the operator did not get their first choice.

reason.description: A closed vocabulary, never prose. A model no adapter maps is a compile ERROR rather than a skip, so 'unmapped' cannot appear in a manifest that exists.

notices.description: Optional-capability gaps: a compile-time WARNING that lands here, because a warning that only reaches stderr is nothing.

realms.description: The map is workspace data, not bundle data: it is pinned here and it is NOT part of the bundle manifest, so adopting a map moves no bundle digest.

source.description: The map file as it was named at invocation. Display and diagnostics only — identity is the digest, and the answer is the embedded content.

sha256.description: sha256 over the CANONICAL JSON of the embedded map, computed exactly like every other digest in this family — so the pin is re-derivable from the embedded content alone, by a reader who no longer has the file.

map.description: The map's content verbatim: a forge.realms/v1 document (contracts/realms.v1.schema.json).
